Given that,
$\cot \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)=\sec \left\{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)\right\}$
Since, $\cos ^{-1} x=\cot ^{-1} \left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right) and $\tan ^{-1} x=\sec ^{-1}$\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)\Rightarrow \cot \left(\cot ^{-1} \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)=\sec  \left\{\sec ^{-1} \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)^2}\right\}\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\sqrt{\frac{b^2-a^2+a^2}{b^2-a^2}}\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\frac{b}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}$On squaring both the sides, we get
 ⇒ $\frac{x^2}{1-x^2}=\frac{b^2}{b^2-a^2}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow& x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2-b^2 x^2 \\ & x^2 b^2+b^2 x^2-x^2 a^2=b^2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad 2 x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2 \Rightarrow x^2\left(2 b^2-a^2\right)=b^2\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{b}{\sqrt{2 b^2-a^2}}$

questions.q: The value of $\cos  \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)$ at $x=\frac{1}{5}is$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos \left[2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\pi / 2\right]=-\sin \left[\cos ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =-\sin \left[\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{1-x^2}\right]=-\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ & =-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}=-\sqrt{\frac{24}{25}}=-\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $y=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{2}(1+\cos 2 x)+\sqrt{\left(\sin ^2 x-48 \cos ^2 x\right)} \sin x\right)=\cos ^{-1}\left((7 \cos x)(\cos x)+\sqrt{1-49 \cos ^2 x} \sqrt{1-\cos ^2 x}\right)=\cos ^{-1}(\cos x)-\cos ^{-1}(7 \cos x) \quad[\because \cos x < 7 \cos x]=x-\cos ^{-1}(7 \cos x)$

questions.q: The value of $\cos  \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)$ at $x=\frac{1}{5}is$
questions.solution: $\cos \left[2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right]=\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right]=\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right]=-\sin \left[\cos ^{-1} x\right]=-\sin \left[\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right]=-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{2}}=-\sqrt{\frac{24}{25}}=-\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}$

questions.solution:
We have, $\mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{n}{tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2m}{{m}^{4} + {m}^{2} + 2}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{n}{tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\left({m}^{2} + m + 1\right) - \left({m}^{2} - m + 1\right)}{1 + \left({m}^{2} + m + 1\right)\left({m}^{2} - m + 1\right)}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{n}\left[{tan}^{- 1}\left({m}^{2} + m + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}\left({m}^{2} - m + 1\right)\right]$

$= \left({tan}^{- 1}3 - {tan}^{- 1}1\right) + \left({tan}^{- 1}7 - {tan}^{- 1}3\right) + \left({tan}^{- 1} ( 13 ) - {tan}^{- 1}7\right) + \ldots + \left({tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right)\right\left- {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right)\right)$

$= {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}1$

$= {tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2} + n + 1 - 1}{1 + \left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right)}\right) = {tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2} + n}{{n}^{2} + n + 2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $S = \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2n}{n^{4} + n^{2} + 2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $S = \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}{tan}^{- 1}\dfrac{2n}{{n}^{4} + {n}^{2} + 2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Let ${n}^{4} + {n}^{2} + 1 = \left[{\left({n}^{2}\right)}^{2} + {1}^{2} + 2\left({n}^{2}\right)\left(1\right)\right] - {n}^{2}$

$= {\left({n}^{2} + 1\right)}^{2} - {n}^{2}$

$= \left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right)\left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Let ${u}_{n} = {tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2n}{{n}^{4} + {n}^{2} + 2}\right)$ 

$= {tan}^{- 1}\dfrac{2n}{1 + \left({n}^{4} + {n}^{2} + 1\right)}$

$= {tan}^{- 1}\dfrac{\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - \left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right)}{1 + \left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right)\left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right)}$

${u}_{n} = {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right) . . . \left(iii\right)$

On putting $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots \ldots$ successively in Eq. (iii), we get

${u}_{1} = {tan}^{- 1}3 - {tan}^{- 1}1$

${u}_{2} = {tan}^{- 1}7 - {tan}^{- 1}3$

${u}_{3} = {tan}^{- 1}13 - {tan}^{- 1}7$

${u}_{n} = {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} - n + 1\right)$

On adding vertically, we get

$\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}{u}_{n} = {tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}1$

$S = \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}{u}_{n}$   [from Eq. (i)]

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}{tan}^{- 1}\left({n}^{2} + n + 1\right) - {tan}^{- 1}1$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 a}{1+a^{2}}\right)-\cos ^{-1} \left(\frac{1-b^{2}}{1+b^{2}}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^{2}}\right), then what is the value of $ x$ ?$
questions.solution: Given, $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 a}{1+a^{2}}\right)-\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-b^{2}}{1+b^{2}}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^{2}}\right)\therefore \quad 2 \tan ^{-1} a-2 \tan ^{-1} b=2 \tan ^{-1} x\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1} a-\tan ^{-1} b=\tan ^{-1} x\Rightarrow \quad \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a-b}{1+a b}\right)=\tan ^{-1} x\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{a-b}{1+a b}$

questions.q: If $\cos ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} \frac{y}{2}=\alpha$, then $4 x^{2}-4 x y \cos \alpha+y^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\cos ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} \frac{y}{2}=\alpha\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x y}{2}+\sqrt{\left(1-x^{2}\right)\left(1-\frac{y^{2}}{4}\right)}\right)=\alpha\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x y+\sqrt{4-y^{2}-4 x^{2}+x^{2} y^{2}}}{2}\right)=\alpha\Rightarrow 4 x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x y \cos \alpha=4 \sin ^{2} \alpha$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The greatest and least values of $\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}$ are respectively
questions.solution:
We have, $\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}=\left(\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-2 \sin ^{-1} x \cdot \cos ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}-2 \sin ^{-1} x\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin ^{-1} x\right)=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}-\pi \sin ^{-1} x+2\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}=2\left[\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-\frac{\pi}{2} \sin ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi^{2}}{8}\right]=2  \left[\left(\sin ^{-1}x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right]

Thus, the least value is 2 \left(\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right)$ i.e. $\frac{\pi^{2}}{8}$ and the greatest value is $2 \left[   \left(\frac{-\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right]$ i.e. $\frac{5 \pi^{2}}{4} .$
